title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: price increase
drivers.evidence: 6.2% price hike; recent sales at $12.03 were 13 and 24 (vs baseline 18.7), suggesting ~12% demand reduction; noise-adjusted effect from past promotions shows demand drops at higher prices.

drivers.name: supply risk
drivers.evidence: Supplier warning of short delivery; implies potential stockout, reducing actual sales below forecast, especially if inventory is constrained.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.7. A 6.2% price increase to $12.03 is a known demand-lowering driver. Recent weeks show no promotion, but the price spike on 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 saw sales rise to 13 and 24, respectively—above baseline but not unusually so. The noise-adjusted post-promo effect is x1.0, indicating no lasting pull-forward. Supplier delivery warning adds supply risk, lowering confidence. No event or promotion is scheduled. The classical model suggests no uplift, but price increase and supply risk justify downward adjustment. Evidence is thin, so shrink toward 1.0.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.7 | 5%-95%: 4.5 - 37.5 | 10%-90%: 8.2 - 33.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
